### Observed differences

- Broad picture: in the earlier window, A25 was followed by A28 in about 97 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions, A26 ran later in the case (median position about 0.55 versus about 0.40 for A28), and after A26 the process chose either A27 (about 54 in 100 of A26's outgoing transitions) or the group A36/A37/A42, whose three members always ran together in varying order (about 46 in 100); A27 and that group co-occurred in only about 1 in 100 cases. In the later window, virtually every case contained all of A25, A26, A27, A28, A36, A37, A42 and A31, in the shape A25, then the group in varying order, then A28, then A26, then A27, with A31 last. [DIR001, DIR002, REL005, REL009, REL011, REL014, REL020, POS002, POS004]

- Participation: A27 ran in about 55 in 100 cases earlier and in all 200 later-window cases; A36, A37 and A42 each ran in about 46–47 in 100 cases earlier and in about 199–200 of 200 later, in each case about once per case (mean occurrences about 1.0, up from about 0.5). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

- Relocation of the group: earlier, A28 preceded A36, A37 and A42 in the about 46–47 in 100 cases where they met; later, A25 leads to A36, A37 and A42 in roughly equal thirds (about 31–34 in 100 each), each group member precedes A28 in about 97–99 in 100 cases, and the group's median position moved from about 0.59 of the case to about 0.41 while A28's moved from about 0.38 to about 0.46. [DIR001, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL014, REL015, REL016, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008]

- Routing at A26 and A27's new context: A26's outgoing transitions changed from a roughly 54/46 split between A27 and the group to about 98 in 100 to A27; the group now precedes A26 (A36 before A26 in about 98–99 in 100 cases, versus A26 first in about 46–47 in 100 earlier), A26 precedes A27 (about 97 in 100, versus about 54 in 100 earlier), A28 precedes A27 (about 97 in 100 later), and A27 still precedes A31 (about 54 in 100 cases earlier, about 97–98 in 100 later). [DIR002, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]

- Exits and internal order: earlier, each of A36, A37 and A42 led to A31 in about 29–34 in 100 of its outgoing transitions; in the later window such transitions are no longer observed, and each member instead leads to A28 in about 31–34 in 100 transitions. A31 itself ran in every case in both windows, with the group before it (co-occurrence about 46 in 100 earlier, about 99 in 100 later) and a slightly later position (median about 0.64 to 0.67). Within the group, order stayed unfixed in both windows, each pair order occurring in roughly half of the cases. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, REL022, POS005]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the exclusive branch after A26 was replaced by a fixed sequence: the group A36, A37, A42 — previously an alternative to A27, running together in about 46 in 100 cases — is now executed in every observed case and is placed directly after A25 and before A28, while A27, previously taken after A26 in about 54 in 100 cases, now runs in every observed case after A26. This is shown directly by relational and successor evidence — co-occurrence of A27 with each group member rising from about 1 in 100 to about 99–100 in 100, the group following A25 and preceding A28 and A26 in about 97–99 in 100 cases, A25's transitions shifting from about 97 in 100 to A28 into thirds leading into the group, and A26's shifting from the 54/46 split to about 98 in 100 to A27 — with the participation and position indicators consistent across all 39 qualifying items, far more than the roughly 0.64 expected for an unchanged process. The many agreeing items largely describe one and the same relocation rather than independent confirmations, and a competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the two windows draw different mixes of pre-existing case types rather than reflecting a modified process; the internal order of A36, A37 and A42 also remains unfixed, so the evidence shows a relocated block, not a newly fixed order within it. [DIR001, DIR002, REL006, REL009, REL011, REL014, OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]

Other differences: in the later window, small outgoing shares of about 0.5–1 in 100 appear at A25, A26, A36, A37 and A42 towards various activities, and A27, A36 or A37 repeat within a case in about 1–3 in 100 cases, which was not observed earlier; A25's position is marginally earlier (mean about 0.37 to 0.35). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, POS001]
